featured_reviews.name: Liviu-Alexandru Buftea (Style)
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you found this place, you had a good guide!

I thought it was Portuguese, but it's actually British. Black as the basaltic rock that rises from the sea, Worli Fort gives a great overview of the bay and the city. It features the classic crenelations and ramparts of the 17th century, and guards the golf from the tip of this tongue of land.

The fort now is not officially maintained or "open to the public". In fact, it seems even locals don’t know about it, but my friend brought me here cause she heard it’s nice. It is accessible for explorer types, and is basically left abandoned.

The fort is simply used by people in this neighborhood for storage, hang out, kids play space, etc. Some clothes left out to dry on the sides, and some barrels and stuff in the rooms below.

Here we met a couple of guys from the city, chilling, listening to cool music, they welcomed us to chat.

It smelled of sea salt, soap, garbage, fish and rats, and the breeze brought “fresh” air from the sea.

As a first time visitor in India, I was in culture shock. Seeing everything was kind of like a dreamy, surreal landscape. So I probably romanticized it too much, for the place is a slum surrounded by a garbage dump, and people here have little chance to better their days, but they were happy, kind and curious.

It was an interesting and humbling experience, worth respect.

featured_reviews.name: Rohan Singh
featured_reviews.review_text: This is the one of the best place to have mumbai's view, only drawback I noticed was connectivity from metro, etc, still it is walkable if alone or not with family, you will have to cross koliwada but the road is good must go in good rainy weather clear sunset time.

featured_reviews.name: Disha Bhatt
featured_reviews.review_text: This is the best experience. After the narrow lanes of Worli Koliwada village, you can reach here, and the best thing you can see is the view.

featured_reviews.name: Hr Patil
featured_reviews.review_text: Worli Fort and Worli Koliwada offer a beautiful mix of Mumbai’s history, culture, and sea views. The fort gives a peaceful vibe with stunning views of the Bandra-Worli Sea Link, especially during sunset. The narrow lanes of Worli Koliwada showcase the authentic charm of Mumbai’s fishing community and local lifestyle. It’s a great place for photography, exploring hidden corners of the city, and enjoying calm moments away from the busy streets. The atmosphere feels raw, real, and deeply connected to Mumbai’s heritage. Definitely worth visiting if you enjoy historic places and scenic coastal views.

featured_reviews.name: PratikG. Naik
featured_reviews.review_text: Historical place but due to surroundings are not well maintained, it lost its natural beauty. The fort walls are still in good conditions. If you ar visiting worli village you can visit atleast one time.

featured_reviews.name: Manish Kumar Verma
featured_reviews.review_text:
Worli Fort offers a serene view of the Arabian Sea and Bandra-Worli Sea Link. Though the fort is small and not very well maintained, the location is scenic and perfect for a quiet sunset. A good place for photography and some quiet reflection. Best visited in the early morning or late evening. Limited parking and cleanliness could be improved.
The way to the fort is a narrow lane that passes through the dirty slum houses !

featured_reviews.review_text: Malad Fish Market is a large, busy seafood market in Malad West, just a short walk from Malad railway station (West) on Sainath Road, and is popular for fresh, relatively low-priced sea fish. Location and access Located on Sainath Road, very close to Malad Railway Station (West); it is  2–5 minutes from the station. Timings  roughly 6:00 am onwards; morning hours are the main time when the wholesale and freshest stock comes.Locals recommend going around 6:00–7:30 am if you want the best catch and prices, especially if buying in bulk. Market layout and what you getThe market is divided into multiple sections: unloading/wholesale area on the road, a covered retail area where they also clean and cut, and open sections where you buy and then pay extra at cutting counters. You typically get a wide variety of saltwater fish like pomfret, surmai, bangda, bombil, prawns, crabs and seasonal catch, with both retail and wholesale options. Tips for visiting Go early, carry change, and be ready to bargain hard; prices are better if you buy in larger quantities.It is a traditional wet market, so expect crowds, strong smell, and wet floors. simple washable footwear and carrying your own bags can be more comfortable.If you tell what exactly you want (pomfret, prawns, bulk/retail, specific budget),

featured_reviews.name: Rajib Saarkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Fish Market at Four Bunglow is one of the most authentic and vibrant seafood destinations in the city. If you’re a seafood lover, this place is a treasure trove. The market comes alive early in the morning with a wide variety of freshly caught fish, prawns, crabs, and even rare seasonal catches that you won’t easily find in supermarkets. The stalls are well-organized, and many vendors are friendly, knowledgeable, and willing to clean or cut the fish as per your requirement, which makes the whole experience convenient.

What stands out most is the freshness—there is a noticeable difference in taste compared to store-bought seafood. Prices are also quite reasonable, and with some bargaining, you can get excellent deals, especially if you’re buying in bulk. Regular customers often know which vendors offer the best catch of the day, so it’s worth exploring a bit before making your pick.

The market does get crowded during peak hours, especially weekends, but that adds to the bustling, energetic vibe. A pro tip is to go early in the morning to get the best selection. Since it’s a traditional fish market, be prepared for the typical sights, sounds, and smells, but that’s part of its charm and authenticity.

Overall, the Fish Market at Four Bunglow is not just a place to buy seafood—it’s an experience in itself. Freshness, variety, and local flavor all come together here, making it a must-visit for seafood enthusiasts.

With the choice of fishes ranging more than 100 varieties in fresh water, 25 in marine and over 50 different types of aquatic plantations, you can certainly deck up your aquarium with some of the exotic range of items. In addition to this we also specialize in the manufacturing of custom-designed fish tanks of all shapes and sizes as per your room plan. So, if you are planning to set-up an aquarium at your home or office, Sheetal Aquarium holds the expertise to design the entire structure as per your budget. To make things easier and hassle-free at your end, we offer a host of maintenance plans to look after your aquatic system.

featured_reviews.name: Ruturaj Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
The attendant is rude. Has zero information about fishes.
.she gave all female gouramis...out of 4 , two died due to infighting
Tanks full of overcrowding

.not at all courteous staff

featured_reviews.name: Tyronne Nunes
featured_reviews.review_text: Amazing collection of fresh water and marine fishes.. good quality fish food and accessories. They also do AMC’s. Staff are very friendly and helpful.

featured_reviews.name: Jaideep Gawade
featured_reviews.review_text: Worst experience I told the owner for motor details he didn’t send me that details 3 days. After that I was visited there shop one wrass fish I want they didn’t get out for there fish tank atleast 2 weeks after that they sold to someone

featured_reviews.name: Elton Pereira
featured_reviews.review_text: Excellent collection of marine fishes. Get good quality fishes at reasonable price. The owner is very knowledgeable and gives good experience on how to go about.

featured_reviews.name: Vyomma Mehta
featured_reviews.review_text:
Good fish collection.
Very bad service. The staff is rude.
The kid working there who gets the fish out of their tank is nice. But the maybe managers of the place are rude and honestly disinterested.
We were a group of four who went to buy. He literally asked me to wait outside because he said two of us are already here and instructing.

featured_reviews.name: Aaliya Khan
featured_reviews.review_text: DO NOT FOOL YOURSELVES. I gave the owner the order & showed him multiple pictures of the particular fish tank i wanted to be made. He confidently said we will make it and asked me to transfer 10k as advance and I did. These people are extremely unprofessional they don’t answer your phone call on time after receiving the amount and I had to go to there shop after seeing the fish tank i told him this is not what i asked for so he started putting the blame on me that i came at the wrong place. I lost 7200/- inr because of these fools. They robbed me of their own mistake.

featured_reviews.name: Atharva Chavan
featured_reviews.review_text: Worst experience. I took a heater from this shop for 300rs and in just one day it stopped working and water went inside that heater . So i went there to replace he told me that he cannot replace that piece and he showed me different heater for 150rs I took that but that also didn't work . Waste of money and time.

featured_reviews.name: Porus Sinor
featured_reviews.review_text: Very good selection of marine fish.. very few fresh water fish like goldfish or kois.. reasonable prices for accessories... Main business is home aquarium cleaning services ...

featured_reviews.name: Ajay
featured_reviews.review_text: One of the oldest fish market in Mumbai. All kinds and variety of sea fishes including Pomfret, Halwa, Bombay duck, Surmai, Prawns, Shell fish, Crabs, Bangda etc available. You also get dry fish in this market. The most important thing is all those options are available in your budget.

featured_reviews.name: Ajinkya Tawde
featured_reviews.review_text: One of the oldest Fish Markets providing all kinds of fish and meat products right from cheapest affordable ones to all deep pocket ones... usually heavily crowded n Sundays...one will get all sorts of fish here...there are lots of sellers behind a narrow lane inside the market as well...even Chicken and Mutton shops there inside...

featured_reviews.name: Raja Sen
featured_reviews.review_text: The chick is injected with water- beware. Ra.200 per kilogram. The fish is fresh and good, although prices are on the higher side. The vendor will clean and cut the fish as per your wishes.

featured_reviews.name: Sagar
featured_reviews.review_text: Definitely a crowded fish market but you will find fresh fish for sure. Famous fish lady is Meenatai seats at backside and she deals in big and costly fishes.

featured_reviews.name: Prof Ramakant DG
featured_reviews.review_text: As name  Fish are available. but if you enter one can find small shops for ladies and kids toys.which also famous and essie access shops for parel,bhoiwada,naigaon etc.But if you really interested in Fish then may be disappointing here as only few sellers.You can also get chicken,goat meat here.

featured_reviews.name: SACHIN KUMAR
featured_reviews.review_text: A variety of fish is available here aling with fresh water fish . You can get crabs, prawns, snails and a lot of fresh sea food items at affordable price

featured_reviews.name: Rohit Bhavar
featured_reviews.review_text: Godd place to buy fishes in n Parel area, however some more efforts can take you to Bhaucha dhakka for fresh and cheaper fishes.

featured_reviews.name: Amogh T.
featured_reviews.review_text: One of the many fish markets in Dadar, this is easily on of the biggest. Has a lot of options - fish, crabs, prawns and even chicken shops.
